readers.title: Pat the Cat
readers.setName: CVC Readers (Short Vowels Only)
readers.phonicsFocus: Short a with simple consonants (c, m, p, t, s, n)

pages.text: Pat sat.
The cat sat.
Pat pat the cat.
The cat naps.

readers.title: Big Pig
readers.setName: CVC Readers (Short Vowels Only)
readers.phonicsFocus: Short i with consonants (b, d, g, h, p, w)

pages.text: The pig is big.
The pig digs.
The pig is in a pit.
Dig, dig, dig!

readers.title: Hot Dog
readers.setName: CVC Readers (Short Vowels Only)
readers.phonicsFocus: Short o with consonants (d, g, h, j, l, p, t)

pages.text: The dog is hot.
The dog jogs.
A pot is hot.
Hop in, dog!

readers.title: Bud the Pup
readers.setName: CVC Readers (Short Vowels Only)
readers.phonicsFocus: Short u with consonants (b, d, g, j, m, p, r, s)

pages.text: Bud is a pup.
The pup dug.
Bud jumps up.
Run, run, Bud!

readers.title: Red Hen
readers.setName: CVC Readers (Short Vowels Only)
readers.phonicsFocus: Short e with consonants (b, h, n, p, r, t)

pages.text: The hen is red.
The red hen pets a pet.
Ten hens in a pen.
The red hen gets the net.

readers.title: Chip and Chop
readers.setName: Digraph Readers (CVC + Digraphs)
readers.phonicsFocus: ch digraph with CVC review

pages.text: Chip is a chipmunk.
Chop is a chipmunk.
Chip and Chop chat.
The chipmunks munch chips.
Chip and Chop run to the den.

readers.title: Fish Wish
readers.setName: Digraph Readers (CVC + Digraphs)
readers.phonicsFocus: sh digraph with CVC review

pages.text: I wish for a fish.
The fish is in a dish.
Shh! The fish swish and dash.
I can wash the fish dish.
A fish in a shop!

readers.title: This and That
readers.setName: Digraph Readers (CVC + Digraphs)
readers.phonicsFocus: th digraph (voiced and unvoiced) with CVC review

pages.text: This is a path.
That is a bath.
I think this is thick.
That moth is thin.
This and that!

readers.title: Duck Luck
readers.setName: Digraph Readers (CVC + Digraphs)
readers.phonicsFocus: ck spelling pattern with short vowels

pages.text: The duck had luck.
Rick the duck got a sock.
Nick the duck got a rock.
The ducks kick and quack.
Pick a duck!

readers.title: Ring a Song
readers.setName: Digraph Readers (CVC + Digraphs)
readers.phonicsFocus: ng and nk digraphs with CVC review

pages.text: I sing a song.
Ding, dong, ding!
The king can sing and bang the gong.
I think pink is long.
Sing along to the song!

readers.title: Frog on a Log
readers.setName: Initial Blend Readers (CVC + Digraphs + Initial Blends)
readers.phonicsFocus: R-blends (fr, gr, br, cr, tr) with digraphs

pages.text: A green frog sits on a log.
The frog hops from the log to a rock.
A crab grabs the frog!
The brave frog croaks and trips back.
The frog grins on the fresh grass.

readers.title: Sled Fun
readers.setName: Initial Blend Readers (CVC + Digraphs + Initial Blends)
readers.phonicsFocus: L-blends (sl, bl, cl, fl, gl, pl) with digraphs

pages.text: The black sled slides.
Flip flops on the sled.
Bliss claps as she sleds.
The sled glides and slips.
A glad clan sleds on the flat hill!

readers.title: Snack Stop
readers.setName: Initial Blend Readers (CVC + Digraphs + Initial Blends)
readers.phonicsFocus: S-blends (sn, sp, st, sk, sm, sw) with digraphs

pages.text: Stan stops at the snack shop.
He sniffs the fresh snacks.
Stan spots chips and a crisp snap stick.
The snacks smell grand!
Stan skips with the bag to swim class.

readers.title: Drip Drop
readers.setName: Initial Blend Readers (CVC + Digraphs + Initial Blends)
readers.phonicsFocus: Mixed initial blends with all digraphs

pages.text: Drip, drop, splish, splash!
The spring brings soft drops.
A sprout sprouts from the sand.
A trim track gets slick and slips.
The fresh grass and clams drink the drips!

readers.title: Trent and Brent
readers.setName: Initial Blend Readers (CVC + Digraphs + Initial Blends)
readers.phonicsFocus: Comprehensive initial blends review

pages.text: Trent and Brent are chums.
The pals grab the swings and spin fast.
Brent trips, but he grins.
Trent helps Brent stand and brush off.
Glad pals skip from the swings to the track!

readers.title: Camp Quest
readers.setName: Final Blend Readers (All Previous Patterns + Final Blends)
readers.phonicsFocus: Final blends (mp, st, nd, nt, nk) with all previous patterns

pages.text: Grant went to camp last spring.
He slept in a tent and felt the crisp wind.
The camp had a fast hunt for frogs and fish.
Grant stomp, stomp, stomped on the path at dusk.
He thinks camp was the best and wants to go back next summer!

readers.title: The Stamp Shop
readers.setName: Final Blend Readers (All Previous Patterns + Final Blends)
readers.phonicsFocus: Final blends (st, mp, ft, pt) with initial blends and digraphs

pages.text: The stamp shop on Elm Street is grand.
Mrs. Frost kept old stamps from the past.
She swept the shop and stacked the stamps with help.
The stamps cost a lot, but Kent still spent his funds.
He left the shop with soft stamps of ducks and plants!

readers.title: Kind Skunk
readers.setName: Final Blend Readers (All Previous Patterns + Final Blends)
readers.phonicsFocus: Final blends (nk, nd, nt, ft, lt) with all patterns

pages.text: A skunk went past the pond to find a pal.
The skunk felt sad, but then he met a kind chipmunk.
The chipmunk did not mind the scent and did not shrink back.
The chums held hands and sang next to the sandbox.
The skunk grinned and felt glad at last!

readers.title: Band Land
readers.setName: Final Blend Readers (All Previous Patterns + Final Blends)
readers.phonicsFocus: Final blends (nd, nt, st, mp, ft) with complex sentences

pages.text: In Band Land, the grand band must help the king.
The band held trumpets, drums that went thump, and long flutes.
The band spent the day next to the sand drifts practicing songs.
The king felt glad and clapped when the band burst into the grand tent.
At last, the band went to the next land to present a gift of music!

readers.title: West Wind Quest
readers.setName: Final Blend Readers (All Previous Patterns + Final Blends)
readers.phonicsFocus: Comprehensive review of all final blends, initial blends, and digraphs

pages.text: The west wind swept across the vast land and bent the plants.
Swift, the smallest elf, felt the wind and had a bold plan to find its path.
Swift drank from his flask and kept his quest strong, jumping past hills and ponds.
At the crest of the last bluff, Swift met the west wind at the end.
The west wind was just a soft draft, and Swift grinned as he held the secret of the wind quest at last!
